metadata.title: A Potential Energy Diagram Shows Where a Particle Cannot Go
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: A particle slides back and forth in a valley. Why can it never pass certain points?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A particle slides back and forth along a frictionless track, climbing partway up each side of a valley before sliding back. Nothing on the track seems to stop it, yet there are points it can never pass.
beats.new_visual_element: A grey valley-shaped track with hatched ground beneath; a gold particle slides back and forth along it, climbing partway up each side.

beats.narration_text: On this track, the particle's potential energy is its weight times its height. So a graph of potential energy against position, U of x, has exactly the shape of the track itself.
beats.new_visual_element: The particle fades; the track morphs into the curve U(x) on position and energy axes, same silhouette.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: axes (x, energy) with valley-shaped curve U(x)

beats.narration_text: With no friction, the total mechanical energy, E, kinetic plus potential, stays constant. On the same graph, that energy is a flat horizontal line, crossing the curve at two points.
beats.new_visual_element: A dashed teal horizontal line E is drawn across the graph; two black dots mark where it crosses U(x).
beats.accumulated_scene_state: U(x), constant-E line, two crossing points

beats.narration_text: The kinetic energy at any position is E minus U of x. Wherever the curve rises above the line, the kinetic energy would have to be negative, which is impossible, because kinetic energy is one half m v squared. Those regions are forbidden.
beats.new_visual_element: Card: K = E − U(x). A teal bar between curve and line at an allowed position, labeled K; a vermilion bar where U(x) > E, labeled K < 0. Card adds U(x) > E ⇒ K < 0; both outer regions beyond the crossing points shade translucent vermilion.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: U(x), E line, crossing points, equation card, K bars, two shaded forbidden zones

beats.narration_text: So the particle oscillates between the two crossing points. It slows as it climbs, stops exactly where U equals E, and turns back. These are the turning points, and the particle never goes beyond them.
beats.new_visual_element: Card and static bars clear. The gold particle reappears on the curve and oscillates between the crossing points; a teal bar from the curve up to the E line rides with it, shrinking to zero at each turning point. The dots are labeled turning point.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: U(x), E line, forbidden zones, oscillating particle with its K bar, turning point labels

beats.narration_text: The potential energy diagram does more than describe the motion. Together with the total energy, it marks out exactly where the particle is allowed to go.
beats.new_visual_element: Particle rests at the left turning point; beneath the graph: Classically forbidden: U(x) > E.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: curve, E line, forbidden zones, particle at a turning point, summary label
